caption: Primary route direction sign
colour: Green background, white lettering and borders, yellow route numbers
explanation: A green direction sign shows the way along a primary route (a major 'A' road of national or regional importance); follow it for the place name or route number you want.
mnemonic: Green = Go the main way (primary 'A' roads).
searchTerms: green road sign with place names
notes: Composite: drawn in-app. Primary-route direction signs are flexible per-junction assemblies of place names, route numbers and arrows (TSRGD Schedule 12 working-drawing signs), not a single fixed-artwork diagram. The Highway Code illustrates them with photographs (e.g. direction-sign-green-approach-to-junction.jpg), and Commons has no generic 'primary route direction sign' SVG. Colour confirmed via gov.uk Highway Code: green background, white lettering, yellow route numbers.

caption: Non-primary route direction sign
colour: White background, black lettering, route numbers and black border
explanation: A white direction sign with black text shows the way along a non-primary route (a local road, including some 'A' and 'B' roads); follow it for your destination.
mnemonic: White and plain = the local, non-primary lane.
notes: Composite: drawn in-app. Non-primary route direction signs are per-junction assemblies of place names, route numbers and arrows, not a single fixed diagram; Highway Code shows them photographically (white ground, black legend, black border). No generic SVG on Commons. Note diagram 824-G-L/825-G-L exist but are the green '200/100 yards to next exit' countdown markers, not the generic white direction sign.

caption: Tourist attraction sign
colour: Brown background, white lettering and symbol
explanation: A brown sign with white text or symbol points the way to a tourist attraction or facility; follow it only if that is where you are heading.
mnemonic: Brown for a day out of town.
notes: Verified via Commons file page: 'UK traffic sign: Junction ahead leading to a tourist attraction (TSRGDNO 2202)', brown ground, OGL v1.0. This is the canonical example of a brown tourist-attraction direction sign. (Generic multi-destination brown stack signs are otherwise composite, but 2202 is a real single-asset representative.)

caption: Local direction sign
colour: White background, black lettering and border, often small with no route number
explanation: A small white-and-black local direction sign points to nearby places, streets or facilities off the main route; follow it to reach a local destination.
mnemonic: Small and local: nearby names, no big numbers.
notes: Composite: drawn in-app. Local direction signs are per-location assemblies of place/facility names and arrows on a white ground (TSRGD working-drawing signs); no single generic SVG on Commons. Specific niche examples exist (e.g. 2701 'direction to a new housing development') but are not the generic local direction sign taught for CBT.

caption: Route confirmation sign
colour: Green, white or blue background matching the route, with destinations, route numbers and distances
explanation: Sited just after a junction, a route confirmation sign lists destinations ahead with their distances in miles to confirm you are on the right road; read it and carry on.
mnemonic: After the junction it confirms: right road, miles to go.
searchTerms: road sign listing towns and miles
notes: Composite: drawn in-app. Route confirmatory signs are per-route assemblies of destination names, route numbers and distances, coloured to match the route (green primary, white non-primary, blue motorway); no single generic SVG on Commons. Highway Code shows them photographically (e.g. direction-sign-green-route-sign.jpg / direction-sign-blue-route-sign.jpg).
